title: Latency-sensitive launch starter kit
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, operator-friendly starter kit for launching latency-sensitive product paths (chat endpoints, streaming routes, synchronous embeddings) with emphasis on predictable P95/P99 and cost guardrails. It’s intentionally pragmatic — mix of checklist, quick-run KPIs, and traffic shims you can copy into a release runbook.

Context notes (why different):
- Focused on releases where user experience is latency-critical (low-touch chat, interactive tooling).
- Assumes multiple deployment targets: Hosted API + Dedicated pools + optional Private VPC.
- Integrates runtime knobs (batching, cache TTL, quantization profile) with product acceptance metrics.

Quick TL;DR checklist (copy into `go-live`):
- Preflight: model pinned (vX.Y.Z) + inferred kernel profile validated on representative sample (sequence length 128/512)
- Capacity: Dedicated pool commit reserved for launch window (min throughput = X RPS / expected tokens/s)
- SLOs confirmed: P95 < 180ms for warm path; P99 < 420ms for worst-case; error rate < 0.5%
- Canary: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% (each step 60–90m min observation) with automated rollback triggers
- Observability: per-route latency dashboard, cost-per-token stream, model-fallback alerts, KV-cache hit-rate metric instrumented
- Chaos smoke: simulated region loss + model fallback exercised in staging and mirrored in production dry-run

KPI sheet (operational metrics to watch during ramp):
- User-facing: P50/P95/P99 latency (ms), tail latency trend (24h), error rate per route
- Infrastructure: tokens/sec per GPU, avg batch size, queue depth, CPU mem pressure on control-plane agents
- Economics: cost per 1k tokens (hosted), committed GPU utilization (Dedicated), egress cost per region
- Quality: top-100 prompt regression rate, hallucination signal (eval subset), rerank accept rate
- Cache metrics: prefix hit rate, KV-fill latency, warm-up time after restart
- Rollout safety: number of fallbacks in last 24h, region failover count, SLA breach minutes

Thresholds and automated triggers (suggested values you can tune):
- If P95 latency > 200ms for 10m -> throttle non-critical features (lower concurrency), pause next canary step, page oncall
- If error rate > 1% for 5m -> auto-fallback to smaller model variant and open incident (JIRA-PLAT-INC)
- If committed GPU utilization < 40% for 30m after warm-up -> shift traffic or scale down reserved pool (but hold buffer)
- If token cost delta > +20% vs baseline (7d) -> enable Optimize recommendations: lower batch latency target or alternate quant profile

Pre-launch runbook (roles & responsibilities):
- Release lead: Priya Desai — owns canary cadence and go/no-go call
- Infra ops: Ethan Park — verifies Dedicated pool allocations, autoscale policies, region routing policies
- Observability & SRE: Maya Chen — dashboard readiness, alert thresholds, tracing for slow traces
- Model owner: Sofia Alvarez — regression checks, fallback model readiness, quantization artifact
- Customer Success cue: Raj Patel — contact plan for P1 customers if degraded experience observed

Canary plan (detailed):
- Step 0 (staging dry-run): smoke tests (latency, error, cache) + traffic replay of 2k requests/min for 30m
- Step 1 (prod small): 1% traffic for 60m — verify P95, error, cache warm-up. Hold if any threshold crossed
- Step 2 (prod ramp): 10% traffic for 90m — watch queuing metrics, tail latency, average batch size
- Step 3 (broad): 50% traffic for 120m — execute controlled traffic shaping to test autoscaler behavior
- Step 4 (full): 100% with staggered client rollout (10% cohorts every 30m), final verification on cost and UX metrics

Rollback playbook (fast):
- Soft rollback: route traffic to model vX.Y.(Z-1) in weighted routing for immediate tail reduction
- Hard rollback: route entire endpoint to compatible hosted fallback (lower-cost but higher-latency allowed path disabled)
- Infrastructure rollback: reduce concurrency target per GPU and enable additional Dedicated nodes if queue depth spikes

Warm-up and steady-state tricks (to hit latency targets):
- Prefix/KV cache prefill: run synthetic key priming for top N prompt prefixes before traffic cutover
- Warm workers: pre-start 1.2x baseline GPU workers for 10–15m before traffic begins to stabilize KV caches
- Batch shaping: use continuous batching with max_wait tuned to expected RTTs (0–10ms). Prefer smaller batches for interactive flows
- Quantization toggle: prefer int8-fast with A/B test in canary; fallback quant profile must be kept in same model bundle

Post-launch retros (what we collect and why):
- 24h: latency heatmap, most frequent slow prompts, cost delta, any user-reported degradations
- 7d: usage vs forecast, model drift signals, top regressions from eval harness, autoscale events log
- 30d: economics review (cost per active user), adoption rate, capacity commit utilization (dedicated)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to owners):
- (Sofia) final list of 500 canonical prompts for regression harness (deadline: 2026-03-05)
- (Ethan) confirm Dedicated cold-start test window and reservation override process with infra finance (JIRA-PLAT-7821)
- (Maya) add trace-level sampling for one low-latency customer cohort to capture slow-path stack traces
- (Priya) finalize on-call pager thresholds and runbook link in the release calendar by EOD +2

Clipboard snippets (copyable templates):
- Canary-check auto rollback expression (example):
  - trigger = rate(errors[5m]) > 0.01 || increase(p95_latency[10m]) > 20ms -> pause_ramp + page
- Dashboard panel list (minimal):
  - Route health (P50/P95/P99), Requests/sec, Tokens/sec, Avg batch size, KV cache hit%, GPU util, Cost per 1k tokens

Notes to future editors:
- This document is intentionally prescriptive for low-latency launch contexts. For non-interactive large-batch features, prefer larger batch sizes and relaxed P95 targets.
- Keep the quantization artifacts and fallback model bundles in the same model registry entry to simplify rollbacks.

Changelog (short):
- 2025-11-18 created by Priya (starter checklist)
- 2026-01-12 added rollback playbook + thresholds (Maya)
- 2026-02-28 updated CANARY timings and open todos (Ethan)

Slack/comms pointers:
- Prep channel: #prodops-launches, ping @oncall when moving to Step 2 canary
- Post-mortem templates: use /playbooks/launch-postmortem in Confluence and include the `latency_heatmap.csv` artifact

-----
Quick copy list (for runbook inclusion):
- P95 target: 180ms; P99 target: 420ms
- Canary ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% (hold times 60m/90m/120m)
- SRE page triggers: P95 > 200ms for 10m; error rate > 1% for 5m
- Owners: Priya (release), Ethan (infra), Maya (obs), Sofia (model), Raj (cs)

End of starter kit — keep this doc as the short-form checklist you can paste into a release issue.
